1	# Offline scientific material
2	
3	## Image-analysis method
4	
5	Van der Walt et al., “scikit-image: image processing in Python,” *PeerJ* 2,
6	e453 (2014). DOI: [10.7717/peerj.453](https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.453).
7	
8	The paper describes scikit-image as a collection of algorithms for scientific
9	image processing. The supplied source is the `measure` part of the project,
10	which turns a binary or intensity image into geometric and moment-based region
11	measurements.
12	
13	## The supplied microscopy data
14	
15	Muller et al., “Accurate evaluation of size and refractive index for spherical
16	objects in quantitative phase imaging,” *Optics Express* 26(8), 10729--10743
17	(2018). DOI: [10.1364/OE.26.010729](https://doi.org/10.1364/OE.26.010729).
18	
19	The image in `fixtures/cell.png` is the CC0 quantitative-phase cell image
20	distributed by scikit-image. Its documented native pixel spacing is 0.107
21	micrometers. The image is useful here because a microscope image is not merely
22	an array of abstract numbers: the distance represented by one row step and
23	one column step is part of the scientific data.
24	
25	## Coordinate and moment definitions
26	
27	For an image with dimension `D`, let a foreground sample at integer index
28	`i = (i_0, ..., i_{D-1})` have physical coordinate
29	
30	$$
31	x_k = i_k s_k,
32	$$
33	
34	where `s_k` is the sampling interval along axis `k`. If the image has a
35	non-unit intensity value `I(i)`, a raw image moment has the form
36	
37	$$
38	M_p = \sum_i I(i)\prod_k x_k^{p_k},
39	$$
40	
41	where `p` is a multi-index and `|p| = sum(p_k)`. The zeroth moment is the
42	total weight used by the image-moment convention. The centroid is the weighted
43	coordinate obtained from the first-order moments:
44	
45	$$
46	c_k = M_{e_k}/M_0.
47	$$
48	
49	Central moments use the same physical coordinates relative to that centroid:
50	
51	$$
52	\mu_p = \sum_i I(i)\prod_k (x_k-c_k)^{p_k}.
53	$$
54	
55	For a dimensionless normalized descriptor, a common change of measurement unit
56	must not change the answer. A useful convention is therefore to divide the
57	order-`|p|` spatial factor by a common unit scale `u` before applying the
58	mass/area normalization:
59	
60	$$
61	\nu_p = \frac{\mu_p/u^{|p|}}
62	              {M_0^{\,|p|/D+1}}.
63	$$
64	
65	The common scale removes a uniform change of units; the axis-specific values
66	still describe the physical shape of an anisotropically sampled object. In an
67	implementation with no separately supplied physical unit, a
68	deterministic common scale derived from the sampling intervals is needed; the
69	smallest interval is one valid convention because it leaves every interval
70	ratio explicit. The exact array layout and exponent ordering follow the source
71	docstrings and the standard image-moment convention.
72	
73	## Region geometry
74	
75	An inertia tensor is built from second central moments. Its eigenvalues encode
76	the spread of the object along its principal axes, so axis lengths, orientation,
77	and eccentricity must use the same physical coordinate system as the moments.
78	The physical area or volume of a foreground region is its sample count times
79	the product of the axis intervals. Changing the calibration changes metric
80	quantities such as distances and moments, but it does not change which integer
81	lattice sites belong to the segmented object. A conversion from sample
82	identity to physical location therefore has to keep its units explicit.
83	
84	Some raster-boundary quantities are defined by a discrete neighborhood and do
85	not have a generally valid anisotropic interpretation without an explicit
86	geometric model. A scientifically honest implementation may keep such a
87	restriction explicit rather than returning a silently misleading value.
88	
89	## Local documentation supplied with the source
90	
91	The relevant API contracts are in the docstrings of the supplied source,
92	especially the image-moment and region-measurement routines. For background,
93	the project documentation and the current API reference are available at:
94	
95	- https://scikit-image.org/docs/stable/api/skimage.measure.html
96	- https://scikit-image.org/docs/stable/auto_examples/segmentation/plot_regionprops.html

395	def inertia_tensor(image, mu=None, *, spacing=None):
396	    """Compute the inertia tensor of the input image.
397	
398	    Parameters
399	    ----------
400	    image : array
401	        The input image.
402	    mu : array, optional
403	        The pre-computed central moments of ``image``. The inertia tensor
404	        computation requires the central moments of the image. If an
405	        application requires both the central moments and the inertia tensor
406	        (for example, `skimage.measure.regionprops`), then it is more
407	        efficient to pre-compute them and pass them to the inertia tensor
408	        call.
409	    spacing: tuple of float, shape (ndim, )
410	        The pixel spacing along each axis of the image.
411	
412	    Returns
413	    -------
414	    T : array, shape ``(image.ndim, image.ndim)``
415	        The inertia tensor of the input image. :math:`T_{i, j}` contains
416	        the covariance of image intensity along axes :math:`i` and :math:`j`.
417	
418	    References
419	    ----------
420	    .. [1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moment_of_inertia#Inertia_tensor
421	    .. [2] Bernd Jähne. Spatio-Temporal Image Processing: Theory and
422	           Scientific Applications. (Chapter 8: Tensor Methods) Springer, 1993.
423	    """
424	    if mu is None:
425	        mu = moments_central(image, order=2, spacing=spacing)  # don't need higher-order moments
426	    mu0 = mu[(0,) * image.ndim]
427	    result = np.zeros((image.ndim, image.ndim), dtype=mu.dtype)
428	
429	    # nD expression to get coordinates ([2, 0], [0, 2]) (2D),
430	    # ([2, 0, 0], [0, 2, 0], [0, 0, 2]) (3D), etc.
431	    corners2 = tuple(2 * np.eye(image.ndim, dtype=int))
432	    d = np.diag(result)
433	    d.flags.writeable = True
434	    # See https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/aeronautics-and-astronautics/
435	    #             16-07-dynamics-fall-2009/lecture-notes/MIT16_07F09_Lec26.pdf
436	    # Iii is the sum of second-order moments of every axis *except* i, not the
437	    # second order moment of axis i.
438	    # See also https://github.com/scikit-image/scikit-image/issues/3229
439	    d[:] = (np.sum(mu[corners2]) - mu[corners2]) / mu0
440	
441	    for dims in itertools.combinations(range(image.ndim), 2):
442	        mu_index = np.zeros(image.ndim, dtype=int)
443	        mu_index[list(dims)] = 1
444	        result[dims] = -mu[tuple(mu_index)] / mu0
445	        result.T[dims] = -mu[tuple(mu_index)] / mu0
446	    return result

449	def inertia_tensor_eigvals(image, mu=None, T=None, *, spacing=None):
450	    """Compute the eigenvalues of the inertia tensor of the image.
451	
452	    The inertia tensor measures covariance of the image intensity along
453	    the image axes. (See `inertia_tensor`.) The relative magnitude of the
454	    eigenvalues of the tensor is thus a measure of the elongation of a
455	    (bright) object in the image.
456	
457	    Parameters
458	    ----------
459	    image : array
460	        The input image.
461	    mu : array, optional
462	        The pre-computed central moments of ``image``.
463	    T : array, shape ``(image.ndim, image.ndim)``
464	        The pre-computed inertia tensor. If ``T`` is given, ``mu`` and
465	        ``image`` are ignored.
466	    spacing: tuple of float, shape (ndim, )
467	        The pixel spacing along each axis of the image.
468	
469	    Returns
470	    -------
471	    eigvals : list of float, length ``image.ndim``
472	        The eigenvalues of the inertia tensor of ``image``, in descending
473	        order.
474	
475	    Notes
476	    -----
477	    Computing the eigenvalues requires the inertia tensor of the input image.
478	    This is much faster if the central moments (``mu``) are provided, or,
479	    alternatively, one can provide the inertia tensor (``T``) directly.
480	    """
481	    if T is None:
482	        T = inertia_tensor(image, mu, spacing=spacing)
483	    eigvals = np.linalg.eigvalsh(T)
484	    # Floating point precision problems could make a positive
485	    # semidefinite matrix have an eigenvalue that is very slightly
486	    # negative. This can cause problems down the line, so set values
487	    # very near zero to zero.
488	    eigvals = np.clip(eigvals, 0, None, out=eigvals)
489	    return sorted(eigvals, reverse=True)

716	def _props_to_dict(regions, properties=('label', 'bbox'), separator='-'):
717	    """Convert image region properties list into a column dictionary.
718	
719	    Parameters
720	    ----------
721	    regions : (N,) list
722	        List of RegionProperties objects as returned by :func:`regionprops`.
723	    properties : tuple or list of str, optional
724	        Properties that will be included in the resulting dictionary
725	        For a list of available properties, please see :func:`regionprops`.
726	        Users should remember to add "label" to keep track of region
727	        identities.
728	    separator : str, optional
729	        For non-scalar properties not listed in OBJECT_COLUMNS, each element
730	        will appear in its own column, with the index of that element separated
731	        from the property name by this separator. For example, the inertia
732	        tensor of a 2D region will appear in four columns:
733	        ``inertia_tensor-0-0``, ``inertia_tensor-0-1``, ``inertia_tensor-1-0``,
734	        and ``inertia_tensor-1-1`` (where the separator is ``-``).
735	
736	        Object columns are those that cannot be split in this way because the
737	        number of columns would change depending on the object. For example,
738	        ``image`` and ``coords``.
739	
740	    Returns
741	    -------
742	    out_dict : dict
743	        Dictionary mapping property names to an array of values of that
744	        property, one value per region. This dictionary can be used as input to
745	        pandas ``DataFrame`` to map property names to columns in the frame and
746	        regions to rows.
747	
748	    Notes
749	    -----
750	    Each column contains either a scalar property, an object property, or an
751	    element in a multidimensional array.
752	
753	    Properties with scalar values for each region, such as "eccentricity", will
754	    appear as a float or int array with that property name as key.
755	
756	    Multidimensional properties *of fixed size* for a given image dimension,
757	    such as "centroid" (every centroid will have three elements in a 3D image,
758	    no matter the region size), will be split into that many columns, with the
759	    name {property_name}{separator}{element_num} (for 1D properties),
760	    {property_name}{separator}{elem_num0}{separator}{elem_num1} (for 2D
761	    properties), and so on.
762	
763	    For multidimensional properties that don't have a fixed size, such as
764	    "image" (the image of a region varies in size depending on the region
765	    size), an object array will be used, with the corresponding property name
766	    as the key.
767	
768	    Examples
769	    --------
770	    >>> from skimage import data, util, measure
771	    >>> image = data.coins()
772	    >>> label_image = measure.label(image > 110, connectivity=image.ndim)
773	    >>> proplist = regionprops(label_image, image)
774	    >>> props = _props_to_dict(proplist, properties=['label', 'inertia_tensor',
775	    ...                                              'inertia_tensor_eigvals'])
776	    >>> props  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS +SKIP
777	    {'label': array([ 1,  2, ...]), ...
778	     'inertia_tensor-0-0': array([  4.012...e+03,   8.51..., ...]), ...
779	     ...,
780	     'inertia_tensor_eigvals-1': array([  2.67...e+02,   2.83..., ...])}
781	
782	    The resulting dictionary can be directly passed to pandas, if installed, to
783	    obtain a clean DataFrame:
784	
785	    >>> import pandas as pd  # doctest: +SKIP
786	    >>> data = pd.DataFrame(props)  # doctest: +SKIP
787	    >>> data.head()  # doctest: +SKIP
788	       label  inertia_tensor-0-0  ...  inertia_tensor_eigvals-1
789	    0      1         4012.909888  ...                267.065503
790	    1      2            8.514739  ...                  2.834806
791	    2      3            0.666667  ...                  0.000000
792	    3      4            0.000000  ...                  0.000000
793	    4      5            0.222222  ...                  0.111111
794	
795	    """
796	
797	    out = {}
798	    n = len(regions)
799	    for prop in properties:
800	        r = regions[0]
801	        # Copy the original property name so the output will have the
802	        # user-provided property name in the case of deprecated names.
803	        orig_prop = prop
804	        # determine the current property name for any deprecated property.
805	        prop = PROPS.get(prop, prop)
806	        rp = getattr(r, prop)
807	        if prop in COL_DTYPES:
808	            dtype = COL_DTYPES[prop]
809	        else:
810	            func = r._extra_properties[prop]
811	            dtype = _infer_regionprop_dtype(
812	                func,
813	                intensity=r._intensity_image is not None,
814	                ndim=r.image.ndim,
815	            )
816	
817	        # scalars and objects are dedicated one column per prop
818	        # array properties are raveled into multiple columns
819	        # for more info, refer to notes 1
820	        if np.isscalar(rp) or prop in OBJECT_COLUMNS or dtype is np.object_:
821	            column_buffer = np.empty(n, dtype=dtype)
822	            for i in range(n):
823	                column_buffer[i] = regions[i][prop]
824	            out[orig_prop] = np.copy(column_buffer)
825	        else:
826	            if isinstance(rp, np.ndarray):
827	                shape = rp.shape
828	            else:
829	                shape = (len(rp),)
830	
831	            # precompute property column names and locations
832	            modified_props = []
833	            locs = []
834	            for ind in np.ndindex(shape):
835	                modified_props.append(
836	                    separator.join(map(str, (orig_prop,) + ind))
837	                )
838	                locs.append(ind if len(ind) > 1 else ind[0])
839	
840	            # fill temporary column data_array
841	            n_columns = len(locs)
842	            column_data = np.empty((n, n_columns), dtype=dtype)
843	            for k in range(n):
844	                rp = regions[k][prop]
845	                for i, loc in enumerate(locs):
846	                    column_data[k, i] = rp[loc]
847	
848	            # add the columns to the output dictionary
849	            for i, modified_prop in enumerate(modified_props):
850	                out[modified_prop] = column_data[:, i]
851	    return out
852

935	    size), an object array will be used, with the corresponding property name

937	
938	    Examples
939	    --------
940	    >>> from skimage import data, util, measure
941	    >>> image = data.coins()
942	    >>> label_image = measure.label(image > 110, connectivity=image.ndim)

944	    ...                           properties=['label', 'inertia_tensor',

def moments_normalized(mu, order=3, spacing=None):
    """Calculate all normalized central image moments up to a certain order.

    Note that normalized central moments are translation and scale invariant
    but not rotation invariant.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mu : (M,[ ...,] M) array
        Central image moments, where M must be greater than or equal
        to ``order``.
    order : int, optional
        Maximum order of moments. Default is 3.
    spacing : tuple of float, shape (ndim, )
        The pixel spacing along each axis of the image. The central moments
        must have been computed in physical coordinates (i.e. with the same
        sampling intervals). The order-|p| spatial factor of each moment is
        divided by a common unit scale ``u`` before normalization, so that a
        uniform change of measurement unit does not change the result while
        axis-specific values still describe the physical shape of an
        anisotropically sampled object. ``u`` is taken as the smallest
        sampling interval, leaving every interval ratio explicit.

    Returns
    -------
    nu : (``order + 1``,[ ...,] ``order + 1``) array
        Normalized central image moments.

    References
    ----------
    .. [1] Wilhelm Burger, Mark Burge. Principles of Digital Image Processing:
           Core Algorithms. Springer-Verlag, London, 2009.
    .. [2] B. Jähne. Digital Image Processing. Springer-Verlag,
           Berlin-Heidelberg, 6. edition, 2005.
    .. [3] T. H. Reiss. Recognizing Planar Objects Using Invariant Image
           Features, from Lecture notes in computer science, p. 676. Springer,
           Berlin, 1993.
    .. [4] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Image_moment

    Examples
    --------
    >>> image = np.zeros((20, 20), dtype=np.double)
    >>> image[13:17, 13:17] = 1
    >>> m = moments(image)
    >>> centroid = (m[0, 1] / m[0, 0], m[1, 0] / m[0, 0])
    >>> mu = moments_central(image, centroid)
    >>> moments_normalized(mu)
    array([[       nan,        nan, 0.078125  , 0.        ],
           [       nan, 0.        , 0.        , 0.        ],
           [0.078125  , 0.        , 0.00610352, 0.        ],
           [0.        , 0.        , 0.        , 0.        ]])
    """
    if np.any(np.array(mu.shape) <= order):
        raise ValueError("Shape of image moments must be >= `order`")
    if spacing is None:
        spacing = np.ones(mu.ndim)
    nu = np.zeros_like(mu)
    mu0 = mu.ravel()[0]
    # a deterministic common scale derived from the sampling intervals
    u = np.min(spacing)
    for powers in itertools.product(range(order + 1), repeat=mu.ndim):
        if sum(powers) < 2:
            nu[powers] = np.nan
        else:
            nu[powers] = (
                mu[powers]
                / u ** sum(powers)
                / (mu0 ** (sum(powers) / nu.ndim + 1))
            )
    return nu

"""Independent first-principles validation of the repaired moment machinery.

Implements the paper's coordinate definitions directly:
    x_k = i_k * s_k ; M_p = sum I prod x_k^p_k ; c_k = M_e_k/M0
    mu_p = sum I prod (x_k - c_k)^p_k
    nu_p = (mu_p / u^|p|) / M0^(|p|/D + 1), u = min(s)
and compares every moment-derived regionprops property against them on new
inputs: other masks, intensities, dimensionalities, offsets, spacings.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from math import atan2, pi, sqrt
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

TASK_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SOURCE_DIR = TASK_DIR / "source"
sys.path.insert(0, str(SOURCE_DIR))

from skimage.measure import regionprops, regionprops_table  # noqa: E402
from skimage.measure import _moments  # noqa: E402

rng = np.random.default_rng(20240813)
FAILURES = []


def check(name, got, want, rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10):
    got = np.asarray(got, dtype=np.float64)
    want = np.asarray(want, dtype=np.float64)
    if got.shape != want.shape:
        FAILURES.append(f"{name}: shape {got.shape} != {want.shape}")
        return
    if not np.allclose(got, want, rtol=rtol, atol=atol, equal_nan=True):
        FAILURES.append(
            f"{name}: mismatch {got.ravel()[:4]} != {want.ravel()[:4]}"
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reference
def site_axes(shape, spacing):
    return [np.arange(n, dtype=np.float64) * s
            for n, s in zip(shape, spacing)]


def ref_moments(weight, spacing, order=3, center=None):
    """Raw/central moments by direct summation over physical coordinates."""
    n = weight.ndim
    axs = site_axes(weight.shape, spacing)
    if center is not None:
        axs = [a - c for a, c in zip(axs, center)]
    out = np.zeros((order + 1,) * n)
    for powers in itertools.product(range(order + 1), repeat=n):
        acc = 1.0
        for k, p in enumerate(powers):
            if p:
                shape = (-1,) + (1,) * (n - 1 - k)
                acc = acc * axs[k].reshape(shape) ** p
        out[powers] = float(np.sum(weight * acc))
    return out


def ref_centroid(weight, spacing):
    M = ref_moments(weight, spacing, order=1)
    M0 = M[(0,) * weight.ndim]
    return np.array(
        [M[(0,) * k + (1,) + (0,) * (weight.ndim - 1 - k)] / M0
         for k in range(weight.ndim)]
    )


def ref_central(weight, spacing, order=3):
    return ref_moments(weight, spacing, order=order,
                       center=ref_centroid(weight, spacing))


def ref_normalized(mu, spacing):
    n = mu.ndim
    u = min(spacing)
    mu0 = mu[(0,) * n]
    nu = np.full_like(mu, np.nan, dtype=np.float64)
    for powers in itertools.product(range(mu.shape[0]), repeat=n):
        if sum(powers) >= 2:
            nu[powers] = (mu[powers] / u ** sum(powers)
                          / mu0 ** (sum(powers) / n + 1))
    return nu


def ref_hu(nu):
    n = nu
    h = np.empty(7)
    h[0] = n[2, 0] + n[0, 2]
    h[1] = (n[2, 0] - n[0, 2]) ** 2 + 4 * n[1, 1] ** 2
    h[2] = (n[3, 0] - 3 * n[1, 2]) ** 2 + (3 * n[2, 1] - n[0, 3]) ** 2
    h[3] = (n[3, 0] + n[1, 2]) ** 2 + (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3]) ** 2
    h[4] = ((n[3, 0] - 3 * n[1, 2]) * (n[3, 0] + n[1, 2])
            * ((n[3, 0] + n[1, 2]) ** 2 - 3 * (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3]) ** 2)
            + (3 * n[2, 1] - n[0, 3]) * (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3])
            * (3 * (n[3, 0] + n[1, 2]) ** 2 - (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3]) ** 2))
    h[5] = ((n[2, 0] - n[0, 2])
            * ((n[3, 0] + n[1, 2]) ** 2 - (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3]) ** 2)
            + 4 * n[1, 1] * (n[3, 0] + n[1, 2]) * (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3]))
    h[6] = ((3 * n[2, 1] - n[0, 3]) * (n[3, 0] + n[1, 2])
            * ((n[3, 0] + n[1, 2]) ** 2 - 3 * (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3]) ** 2)
            - (n[3, 0] - 3 * n[1, 2]) * (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3])
            * (3 * (n[3, 0] + n[1, 2]) ** 2 - (n[2, 1] + n[0, 3]) ** 2))
    return h


def ref_inertia(weight, spacing):
    """Independent inertia tensor from direct site sums."""
    n = weight.ndim
    axs = site_axes(weight.shape, spacing)
    c = ref_centroid(weight, spacing)
    wsum = weight.sum()
    T = np.zeros((n, n))
    d2 = [((a - c[k]).reshape((-1,) + (1,) * (n - 1 - k))) ** 2
          for k, a in enumerate(axs)]
    for i in range(n):
        spread = sum(weight * d2[k] for k in range(n) if k != i).sum()
        T[i, i] = spread / wsum
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            T[i, j] = T[j, i] = -(weight * (axs[i].reshape((-1,) + (1,) * (n - 1 - i)) - c[i])
                                  * (axs[j].reshape((1,) * j + (-1,) + (1,) * (n - 1 - j)) - c[j])).sum() / wsum
    return T


def embedded(mask, ndim_labels=2, pad_lo=None, pad_hi=None, label=3):
    """Embed mask into a larger label image with nonzero slice offsets."""
    if pad_lo is None:
        pad_lo = [int(rng.integers(0, 7)) for _ in range(mask.ndim)]
    if pad_hi is None:
        pad_hi = [int(rng.integers(0, 7)) for _ in range(mask.ndim)]
    out = np.zeros(tuple(p + m + q for p, m, q
                         in zip(pad_lo, mask.shape, pad_hi)), dtype=int)
    out[tuple(slice(p, p + m) for p, m in zip(pad_lo, mask.shape))] = \
        np.where(mask, label, 0)
    return out, pad_lo


def check_region(rp, mask, spacing, pad_lo, tag, intensity=None,
                 multichannel=False):
    n = mask.ndim
    spacing = tuple(float(s) for s in spacing)
    w = mask.astype(np.float64) if intensity is None else None
    c = ref_centroid(mask.astype(np.float64), spacing)

    check(f"{tag} pixel_area", rp.pixel_area, np.prod(spacing))
    check(f"{tag} area", rp.area, mask.sum() * np.prod(spacing))
    check(f"{tag} area_bbox", rp.area_bbox, mask.size * np.prod(spacing))
    if rp.area_convex:  # ratio-free quantities still exact
        check(f"{tag} area_filled", rp.area_filled,
              np.asarray(rp.image_filled).sum() * np.prod(spacing))
    bbox = [sl.start for sl in rp.slice] + [sl.stop for sl in rp.slice]
    check(f"{tag} bbox", rp.bbox, bbox)
    # coords: integer lattice sites, calibration-independent
    sites = np.argwhere(mask)
    want_coords = sites + np.array(pad_lo)
    check(f"{tag} coords", rp.coords, want_coords)
    # centroid: physical, = local + start * spacing
    check(f"{tag} centroid", rp.centroid, c + np.array(pad_lo) * spacing)
    check(f"{tag} centroid_local", rp.centroid_local, c)
    mu = ref_central(mask.astype(np.float64), spacing)
    check(f"{tag} moments", rp.moments,
          ref_moments(mask.astype(np.float64), spacing))
    check(f"{tag} moments_central", rp.moments_central, mu)
    nu = ref_normalized(mu, spacing)
    check(f"{tag} moments_normalized", rp.moments_normalized, nu)
    if n == 2:
        check(f"{tag} moments_hu", rp.moments_hu, ref_hu(nu))
    T = ref_inertia(mask.astype(np.float64), spacing)
    check(f"{tag} inertia_tensor", rp.inertia_tensor, T)
    ev = sorted(np.linalg.eigvalsh(T), reverse=True)
    check(f"{tag} inertia_tensor_eigvals", rp.inertia_tensor_eigvals, ev)
    if n == 2:
        check(f"{tag} axis_major_length", rp.axis_major_length,
              4 * sqrt(ev[0]))
        check(f"{tag} axis_minor_length", rp.axis_minor_length,
              4 * sqrt(ev[1]))
        ecc = 0 if ev[0] == 0 else sqrt(1 - ev[1] / ev[0])
        check(f"{tag} eccentricity", rp.eccentricity, ecc)
        a, b, _, cc = T.flat
        want_orient = (pi / 4 * (1 if b >= 0 else -1) if a - cc == 0
                       else 0.5 * atan2(-2 * b, cc - a))
        check(f"{tag} orientation", rp.orientation, want_orient)
    elif n == 3:
        check(f"{tag} axis_major_length", rp.axis_major_length,
              sqrt(10 * (ev[0] + ev[1] - ev[2])))
        check(f"{tag} axis_minor_length", rp.axis_minor_length,
              sqrt(10 * (-ev[0] + ev[1] + ev[2])))
    check(f"{tag} equivalent_diameter_area", rp.equivalent_diameter_area,
          (2 * n * rp.area / pi) ** (1 / n))
    check(f"{tag} extent", rp.extent, mask.sum() / mask.size)

    if intensity is not None and not multichannel:
        ii = intensity.astype(np.float64) * mask
        wm = ref_moments(ii, spacing)
        wc = ref_centroid(ii, spacing)
        wmu = ref_central(ii, spacing)
        wnu = ref_normalized(wmu, spacing)
        check(f"{tag} moments_weighted", rp.moments_weighted, wm)
        check(f"{tag} moments_weighted_central",
              rp.moments_weighted_central, wmu)
        check(f"{tag} moments_weighted_normalized",
              rp.moments_weighted_normalized, wnu)
        if n == 2:
            check(f"{tag} moments_weighted_hu", rp.moments_weighted_hu,
                  ref_hu(wnu))
        check(f"{tag} centroid_weighted", rp.centroid_weighted,
              wc + np.array(pad_lo) * spacing)
        check(f"{tag} centroid_weighted_local",
              rp.centroid_weighted_local, wc)


# ------------------------------------------------------------ test battery
def random_mask(shape, blobs=4, fill=0.35):
    m = rng.random(shape) < 0.08
    for _ in range(blobs):
        c = [int(rng.integers(0, d)) for d in shape]
        r = max(float(rng.uniform(2, min(shape) * fill)), 2.0)
        grid = np.indices(shape)
        m |= np.sum((grid - np.array(c)[:, None, None] /
                     rng.uniform(0.7, 1.4, size=(len(shape), 1, 1))) ** 2,
                    axis=0) < r ** 2
    return m


def random_spacing(ndim, aniso=True, scale=1.0):
    lo, hi = 0.05, 2.5
    s = scale * rng.uniform(lo, hi, size=ndim)
    if not aniso:
        s[:] = s[0]
    return tuple(np.round(s * 1000) / 1000)


print("== 2D binary regions, anisotropic spacings, random origins ==")
for trial in range(6):
    mask = random_mask((37, 41))
    lab, pad_lo = embedded(mask)
    spacing = random_spacing(2)
    rp = regionprops(lab, spacing=spacing)[0]
    check_region(rp, mask.astype(bool), spacing, pad_lo,
                 f"2D/t{trial} s={spacing}")

print("== 2D + intensity (single channel) ==")
for trial in range(4):
    mask = random_mask((29, 33))
    intensity = rng.normal(3.0, 1.5, size=mask.shape).astype(np.float64)
    lab, pad_lo = embedded(mask)
    full_int = np.zeros(lab.shape); sl = tuple(slice(p, p + m) for p, m in
                                               zip(pad_lo, mask.shape))
    full_int[sl] = intensity
    spacing = random_spacing(2)

def random_mask(shape, blobs=4, fill=0.35):
    ndim = len(shape)
    m = rng.random(shape) < 0.08
    for _ in range(blobs):

    return m

def tight_slices(mask):
    """Bounding slices of the True content of a boolean array."""
    n = mask.ndim
    out = []
    for ax in range(n):
        anys = mask.any(axis=tuple(k for k in range(n) if k != ax))
        idx = np.flatnonzero(anys)
        out.append(slice(idx[0], idx[-1] + 1))
    return tuple(out)

The repair is complete and verified. Summary:

## Root cause

The workflow calls `regionprops(labels, spacing=(0.107, 0.214))`, and the snapshot's spacing-aware measurement path violated the physical-coordinate convention from the paper (`paper.md`) in six places:

1. **`source/skimage/measure/_moments.py:266` — `moments_normalized` ignored calibration entirely.** Normalized moments were computed as `mu_p / M_0^{|p|/D+1}` on physical central moments, missing the common unit scale, so a uniform change of measurement unit changed the answer. Fixed to accept `spacing` and compute `nu_p = mu_p / u^{|p|} / M_0^{|p|/D+1}` with `u = min(spacing)` — the paper's smallest-interval convention, which keeps axis ratios explicit so the descriptor still describes the anisotropically sampled object.
2. **`_moments.py:248` — `moments_central(center=None)` fell back to `centroid(image)` without spacing**, mixing an index-space center with physical-coordinate deltas. Now `centroid(image, spacing=spacing)`.
3. **`_regionprops.py:408` — `coords` was multiplied by spacing.** Calibration must not change which integer lattice sites belong to the object; `coords` (sample identity) is integer indices again, with the index→physical conversion kept explicit in the metric properties.
4. **`_regionprops.py:596` — `centroid_weighted` added integer `slice.start` to a physical local centroid.** Now `start * spacing`, same as `centroid` (derived from `centroid_local`).
5. **`_regionprops.py:554, 644` — bogus `spacing == (1, 1)` guards on `moments_hu` / `moments_weighted_hu`** made Hu moments "unavailable" for valid calibrated inputs; with correct normalization they are well-defined for any spacing, so the guards were removed (this is why the cell record previously had 3 unavailable properties).
6. Removed the dead `return` line left in `moments_weighted_normalized`.

The `perimeter`/`perimeter_crofton` anisotropy restriction stays — the paper endorses keeping raster-boundary quantities that lack a valid anisotropic interpretation explicitly restricted rather than silently misleading.

## Verification

- **First-principles validation** (`outputs/validate_fix.py`): recomputes every moment-derived property by direct coordinate summation and compares on *new* inputs — random 2D/3D masks, intensity and multichannel images (incl. weighted variants), random slice origins, anisotropic spacings (0.05–2.5 with ratios up to ~50×), multi-label images, stride-subsampled grids (index↔physical representation identity), and uniform unit changes (moments_normalized/Hu/eccentricity/orientation exactly invariant, centroid/area scaling correctly). All pass.
- **Backwards compat** (`outputs/compat_check.py`): with `spacing=None` or `(1, 1)`, the repaired snapshot reproduces stock 0.19.2 values for *every* property and moments function — binary, intensity, multichannel — exactly.
- **Regression sweep**: all 66 stock `test_regionprops.py` + 22 `test_moments.py` tests pass against the repaired snapshot.
- **`python reproduce.py`**: completes with 29/31 properties available (only the two perimeter quantities remain honestly restricted); the cell record now matches independent physical-coordinate calculations, `coords` is `int64` lattice sites, and `centroid = centroid_local + start × spacing` holds exactly.
